sources.note: Bibliographic only: SIL lists James 1990, Rosendall 1992 and Blench 1989 'Nupoid' for gbr; Glottolog lists Weise 2013 and Ethnologue.
Segmental inventories for Gbagyi and Gbari only; no information on tone or stress. References Rosendall 1992, Rosendall 1998, Blench 2013.

sources.citation: Musa, Abigail Dalhatu. 2023. Gbagyi polar question formation: the operations of vowel lengthening and tonal downstepping. Humanity - Jos Journal of General Studies 14(1): 25-30. DOI 10.67862/hjjgs.2023.l9qngqpn
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent on stress. p. 26: 'Gbagyi is a tonal language'; section 3.2 reports Dalhatu (2017): four register tones (Extra High, High, Mid, Low) plus two falling contours; Mid never precedes High.

sources.citation: Adeniyi, Kolawole & Ben Elugbe. 2018. Consonant voicing, tonal morphemes, and downstep in Gwari. Linguistique et langues africaines 4: 77-97. DOI 10.4000/lla.11340
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No mention of stress or accent anywhere in the article. Para. 6: 'Gwari operates a terraced level three-tone system having low (L), mid (M) and high (H) tones (Hyman & Magaji 1971:15) as well as downdrift and downstep'; H realised as rising after L, L as falling after M/H; downstepped M and H.

sources.citation: Muhammad, Aliyu Busa. 2012. A comparative study of Hausa and Gbagyi sound systems. PhD dissertation, Department of African Languages and Cultures, Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria. 136 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Gbagyi stress. Tone sections 2.2.5.3 (pp. 64-65) and 4.1.4 (pp. 82-83): Gbagyi has H, L, M and falling tone patterns (Hyman & Magaji 1970 five tones; Sanda 1986 three; author proposes four). The only occurrence of 'stress' is a general remark (pp. 16-17) that tone, vowel structure, stress and syllabification 'might have been illusive' to non-native authors of earlier Gbagyi books.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger & Musa Doma. 1981-1993 [PDF 2006]. A dictionary of the Gbari language (draft, not tone-marked). Kaduna/Abuja.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Describes Gbari (West Gwari, gby / gbar1246, Kwali-Sumwakpna lect), not Gbagyi proper. Silent on stress. p. 2: 'Gbari is a tone language and every vowel can have one of five possible tones. There are three level tones and two glides, rising and falling'; phonology appendix: 'The tone system of southern Gbari closely resembles both Gbagyi and Northern Gbari.'

sources.citation: Dalhatu, A. 2017. [Extensive study of the Gbagyi tone system; full reference not seen, cited in Musa 2023: 26 as the only extensive study of Gbagyi tone]

sources.note: Most recent full tone analysis of Gbagyi (four register tones + two contours); likely to discuss the absence or presence of stress alongside tone.
